speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Education what measures are in place to prevent sexual harassment in all school settings and what will be done to enhance student protection.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Education what safeguards and measures are in place at institutes of higher learning to (i) protect students from sexual harassment or misconduct and (ii) support affected victims and facilitate case reporting.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung addressed questions relating to the disciplinary frameworks in the institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and the reviews that the IHLs, including the autonomous universities (AUs) are undertaking.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will now address the other questions raised in relation to sexual misconduct in educational institutions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about the prevention of sexual harassment in school settings.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Schools take a firm stand against sexual harassment and exercise judgement to ensure that disciplinary actions reflect the circumstances of each case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Depending on the facts of the case, a Police report may be made.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Beyond disciplinary measures, students are taught to identify risks to their personal safety and learn to seek help from trusted adults, such as their parents and teachers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Teachers are trained to look out for signs of distress and provide victims first-line help.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Both students and teachers are supported by school counsellors and other external agencies, where required.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) works with the schools regularly to ensure that support measures are relevant and effective.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other areas of concern raised by Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap and Mr Leon Perera and which I will now address are what support is currently available in IHLs for the victims of sexual offences and whether it is sufficient, as well as what measures are being taken to ensure a safe environment for all students on campus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In terms of support, the first and most fundamental thing to understand is that sexual misconduct can have a lasting psychological and emotional impact on victims.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The sense of violation and fear that victims, male and female, experience is real and can be crippling.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For many, the road to recovery can be long and painful.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It takes courage for any victim to come forward and report the incident.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There must be strong end-to-end support for victims, starting from the time they step forward to report an incident, to post-incident counselling and psychological support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: NUS has acknowledged this and has committed to doing better.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: NUS is serious about improving its frameworks and processes and has convened a high-level Review Committee to oversee the implementation of various measures by NUS management.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The other IHLs are similarly concerned and are in the process of reviewing their support for victims, with a focus on ensuring that the support provided is holistic, timely and accessible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, some IHLs have in place 24-hour helplines for incident reporting or counselling services.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These ensure that victims or any distressed students receive timely support, even if they come forward outside regular office hours.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As the IHLs do their reviews, there are three broad areas of focus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All the IHLs have full-time counsellors onsite to support victims, as well as a larger group of staff who are trained as para-counsellors to provide additional support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Counsellors are also trained in managing such difficult situations sensitively.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our IHLs will look to strengthening these provisions, taking the victim's entire journey in mind.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The support must extend beyond counselling and begin at the point that the victim first reaches out for help.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We should also ensure victims feel safe to step forward and report cases when they occur and seek help.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: A good support system must create psychological safety for victims, guide them through the processes and protocols involved in the management of their case, update them on investigations and ensure that their concerns and questions are addressed along the entire journey.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All these must be done sensitively and with empathy.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also need to recognise that individuals have different resilience and coping levels and that some of the trauma and stress might not manifest immediately.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For more severe cases, such as sexual assault, our IHLs will need to be equipped to make judgement calls about the victims’ emotional state and quickly call for external professional help where needed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These are important details that will have to be worked out carefully.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, closed-circuit television cameras (CCTVs) complement campus security guards to ensure security in common areas, and some institutions take the additional precautionary measure of having controlled access to female bathrooms and toilets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Additional CCTV cameras are being installed at more locations on campus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: NUS will deploy more security guards at its hostels and introduce roving security patrols across campus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These changes will further strengthen privacy and security on campus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: NUS expects to complete these enhancements in the coming months.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As part of their overall review of campus security, the IHLs will take steps to address new forms of threats, such as the illegal installation of miniature cameras.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, ensuring a collective stand against sexual misconduct in a modern age.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At its core, the issue is about respect for others.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are some who mistakenly think that voyeurism and verbal harassment are not serious because there is no physical contact with the victims.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Voyeurism and other unwanted non-physical harassment exact psychological and emotional harm on victims and, similar to other types of sexual misconduct, have no place in our society.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Perpetrators are no less culpable just because they did not come into physical contact with their victims.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We can and, therefore, must do better to educate students not only on the importance of respect, but also what constitutes harm and violation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Technology has also amplified the potential for harm arising from sexual misconduct.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Institutional processes must, likewise, keep up with the times.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Institutions and organisations must also recognise that expectations of how they should respond are changing, not just in Singapore but globally.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the end of the day, the best deterrent and protection in such cases is if we respect others, both in the physical and emotional space, and conduct ourselves accordingly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think it is good to hear about installing more CCTVs, doors and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If there is, what action is going to be taken to eliminate this deep-rooted culture of sexual harassment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question: I think what we need is education, or even a campaign on zero tolerance towards sexual harassment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, in this aspect, is there anything that can be done?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The first question is whether there is a deep-rooted trend of sexual harassment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sexual harassment is a type of sexual misconduct.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are several types: outrage of modesty, sexual assault, sexual harassment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, I do also acknowledge all the explanations that some of the literature has given, including the "Big Read" article in TODAY that I mentioned earlier, that the young today grow up with the Internet, they are exposed to pornographic websites, they know of miniature photography and recording devices, and sometimes, they get these materials through their WhatsApp.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Over time, they may have the idea that "Actually, this is no big deal".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It has not manifested in terms of higher incidence rates, at least not over the last three years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we do worry about this underlying trend.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do agree with the Member that we need to send a strong signal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It has to be a combination of measures between what I and Second Minister Indranee Rajah have talked about, tougher penalties, education, improving the physical security as well as better support for both the victims as well as, sometimes, for the offenders in counselling them and helping them turn over a new leaf.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I have two questions for Minister Ong Ye Kung.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first is, had this incident not been taken on social media and gained so much attention, would the Ministry and AUs have taken actions to review the disciplinary framework?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second question is, the Minister mentioned that the AUs are now undergoing this full review.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: When they are ready, would the Ministry ensure that the revisions are adequate and serve their purpose?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sorry, I did not catch the Member's first question because I thought we just announced that they would review their framework.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The thing is that if this incident was not taken to social media and had not gained that much attention, would the Ministry and the AUs already have undertaken this review since in the last three years, there was no increase in rates?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Should we not have done this earlier, in other words.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The AUs do review their disciplinary framework from time to time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think what this incident has taught all of us is that there is a stronger concern and also some underlying trends.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we do need to make it tougher at the egregious end of the offence.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think there are many things that we do, sometimes, ahead of time, and we are also being questioned, "Why do you do it now?", "Aren't you going to open up other problems?" In this case, unfortunately, that did not happen.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think what is more important is immediate action is being taken now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am confident that there will be swift and decisive actions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The second question is how we would know if the measures will be adequate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think after this furore, the AUs all understand the implications of this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I have given them my written advice and policy guidance that they have to do a thorough review.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am sure all of them will take it very seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Frankly, I am quite disappointed that the AUs did not take earlier action to review their processes to better deal with the complaints.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am wondering would the Minister review why the AUs did not take further action, having seen the number of cases that have been reported over the three years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If we do not get to the root of the problem, then whatever we do, the AUs will not do anything to review the process until the matter goes up to social media.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can the reported cases of voyeurism be publicised in campus newsletters to alert students of the extent of the problem?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And also, whether the Minister will consider asking the AUs to publicise the punishment of offenders to students in the AUs, so that there is also a learning message for everyone that there is some deterrent effect.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Potential offenders must know that there would be appropriate punishment for them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The first question is again, looking back, why did we not realise that was serious?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Of course, we wish that there was a realisation that these are serious offences.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But having said that, today, after this incident, I believe that the AUs are all very aware and I am confident that they will do something swift and decisive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As to publicising the punishment, NUS has actually been publicising the cases, the sexual misconduct cases and the punishment that has been meted out to them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We just need to toughen them up and send a strong signal that at the most egregious end of the offences, there must be very stiff punishment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have one supplementary question for Second Minister Indranee Rajah.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Minister Indranee Rajah alluded to the infrastructural changes that are happening in the NUS now, the retrofitting of the shower cubicles, the locks, additional security cameras and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is a shame that it took this incident of Ms Monica Baey coming forward before these changes are actually made, given the number of voyeurism offences that have taken place in the previous years.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My supplementary question would be, are these infrastructural changes to enhance security being done across the board for all the IHLs?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And is there a timeframe for this to be carried out?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For the other AUs, they will have to complete their review.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the short answer is that they are all looking at it and their priority is to make sure that the campus is safe for students.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can I ask the Minister, given that this is happening across all the AUs and maybe other IHLs, are we looking to introduce codes and standards to universities and IHLs to help them prevent and manage sexual harassment on campus?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is, are we considering, given the numbers that the Minister has shared, a kind of cross-campus body that would help to manage such incidents?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am wondering because a student does not stay in a university if he has been found to have committed a misconduct or act.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And so, is there this cross-campus sharing of information and, therefore, that warrants a body to be set up?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think the first thing to remember is that it does not take codes and regulations to understand that taking videos of somebody bathing is wrong.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It just needs certain fundamental values, which are that you must respect other people, respect their privacy, respect their physical space, respect their emotional space.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we can, and the AUs will be embarking, as I had mentioned in my earlier response, on better education for the students.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is a function partly of parents, partly schools and teachers and the individual himself or herself.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if you adhere to that, you do not actually need to have codes and regulations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The key thing is really making sure that individuals understand that something like this is not a light offence, is not a light thing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It will be taken seriously, and it will be dealt with seriously and appropriately as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There is also the other aspect which is rehabilitation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In some cases, either they have a problem that needs to be dealt with, and it may require counselling, it may require additional treatment for those who are mentally not well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, that is another aspect that we will be looking at.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I understand that the student in the controversy of this NUS Peeping Tom incident said that he was at the hostel after midnight with the intention to stay over at his girlfriend's hostel room, even though he was not a resident of the hostel.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Would they allow people to go into the hostels after midnight and what is the response from the universities?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The students can and do visit their friends in other hostels.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think that this particular incident will be cause for the universities to reflect on how that arrangement should be managed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Obviously, you do not want to prevent friends from coming to see one another, but the proper recording and the security arrangements for that should be in place.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in short, as a result of this, I think the universities will be reviewing much more closely.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I just want to add that we need to take some firm measures but be careful not to overreact to the extent of not allowing students to visit one another or staying over.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think we can have a lively campus without having all the dangers and security lapses, which we will tighten up.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I appreciate the discretion that the respective AUs have to review their procedures in the light of Monica Baey's ordeal.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is to send that strong signal that the Minister referred to.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, for us to issue standards or codes or rules to the universities would not be appropriate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We can do that for polytechnics because they are Statutory Boards, and we can do that for ITE.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But for AUs, they are differently incorporated and structured.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am sure we will work together, not by MOE issuing rules and regulations but through discussion, moral suasion, I am sure we can come up with something feasible, workable and effective.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The first is on the issue of standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Then, there would be a sense of injustice that the universities differ significantly on the standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And that is why I think it is important that MOE to come in with this suasion and coordinated approach.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They are not professional adjudicators or finders of facts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, what can the Ministry do here to ensure that these committees have the skills necessary to interview the parties concerned, to investigate and to assure the public that justice is being done here?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Different AUs may well have slightly different disciplinary actions, just as different companies would have different disciplinary actions when there are offences.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Having said that, researchers and academics stick to the discipline of peer review very closely and I have no doubt in this aspect that there will be some peer review going on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But of course, if they need enforcement or legal advice, I am sure they can ask for it and they are able to tap on it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: After all, it is a university; lots of different talent in different expertise.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we need to give them some time, some space, to get their work done.
